text: I talked to the sober friend a lot afterwards, which helped me understand that nobody was judging me. I did a few sessions with a therapist on social anxiety. I go to small gatherings now and leave when it gets too much.

Ich habe eine Psychotherapie gemacht, in der ich gelernt habe, die Grübelschleifen zu unterbrechen. Außerdem habe ich mit Sport angefangen, vor allem Laufen, weil mich das aus dem Kopf holt. Gespräche mit einem Freund, der Philosophie studiert, haben mir geholfen, die Fragen weniger bedrohlich zu sehen. Heute geht es mir gut, aber ich nehme keine Psychedelika mehr.

I've tried a lot of things over five years. The most helpful has been a psychologist who specialises in depersonalisation. She helped me understand that the impostor feeling is a symptom, not a truth, and that monitoring it makes it worse. We work a lot on reducing my checking behaviours, like looking at my ID card. I'm down to doing it once in a while.

I tried several medications: two SSRIs, lamotrigine, and naltrexone. Lamotrigine helped somewhat with the intensity. I'm still on it.

Grounding techniques help in the moment: cold water on my face, strong mints, naming objects. Running helps. Playing music helped once I got back to it, though the first months back in the band were hard.

T, my old housemate, has stayed a close friend. Talking to him about that night, and about ordinary things, still helps.

What didn't help: R's insistence that I'd had a spiritual awakening, and forums where people describe DP as permanent.

I'm functional and mostly okay, but it's still there.
Breathing exercises and slowly going to parties again with a friend who knew. It worked, mostly.

Ich habe mir selbst Unterstützung gesucht, bei einer Beratungsstelle für Angehörige von Menschen in psychischen Krisen. Das hat mir geholfen, meine eigene Angst ernst zu nehmen und nicht nur auf ihn zu schauen. Er hat eine Therapie angefangen, und wir haben ein paar Paargespräche gemacht. Heute geht es uns beiden besser.

It took me a year to realise that what she did was a serious boundary violation. A friend who is a psychologist helped me name it. I reported her to the professional board, which was a long and draining process. They took my complaint seriously and she is no longer allowed to practise. I then found a new therapist, a man, which felt safer for me, and we've been working on trust, on the confusion, and on the depression. I was on an antidepressant for a year. I'm much better but it took a long time to be able to sit in a therapy room without feeling unsafe.
Stopped research chems, antihistamine cream for the itching, time.
Didn't need anything, just sorted out the bank stuff.

Ich habe mit einer Psychologin gesprochen, die Erfahrung mit Notfallpsychologie hat. Die Albträume sind dadurch weniger geworden. Mit meinem Freund, der gestürzt ist, habe ich viel geredet, er ist mir nicht böse, im Gegenteil. Vor kurzem bin ich zum ersten Mal wieder in den Bergen gewesen, mit ihm zusammen. Das war ein wichtiger Schritt.

I was very ashamed and didn't want to tell anyone at work. But my GP noticed how bad I was and referred me to an occupational health service, which connected me with a psychologist for healthcare workers. I've been seeing her for two years. We started with stabilisation and grief work about my mother, and later moved to EMDR on the ICU images. That has helped, slowly.

I've been on an antidepressant for two years, and briefly on a sleeping pill.

A peer support group for nurses who worked through the pandemic has been very important. Many of us carry the same rows of faces, even without ayahuasca.

I tried to talk to the retreat leader about what happened. He insisted that I'm a healer and should come back. I blocked him.

I'm not back in the ICU and I don't think I will be. Outpatient work suits me now.
